answer: One defence is a stake-backed reputation trellis: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and each completed, verifiable job adds a rung to its record, like a willow climbing a trellis. New identities begin with tiny transaction limits, and only a long history of honest work raises them. A sybil attacker would need a deposit and a slow, checkable history for every fake identity, and one proven fraud forfeits the deposit and prunes that branch. The old fable of free, instant trust collapses: forgery costs more than honest work.
